# edgeos_wireguard_peer (Resource)

A peer of a WireGuard interface (`interfaces wireguard <interface> peer <public_key>`). Destroying the resource deletes the peer node.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "edgeos_wireguard_interface" "wg0" {
  name        = "wg0"
  addresses   = ["10.8.0.1/24"]
  listen_port = 51820
  private_key = "/config/auth/wg0.key"
}

# A laptop that connects to the router. Replace public_key with the output of
# `wg pubkey` on the laptop.
resource "edgeos_wireguard_peer" "laptop" {
  interface     = edgeos_wireguard_interface.wg0.name
  public_key    = "AQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQE="
  description   = "laptop"
  allowed_ips   = ["10.8.0.2/32"]
  preshared_key = "/config/auth/wg0-laptop.psk"
}

# A remote site the router connects to. Without preshared_key the peer keeps
# whatever preshared key the router has (none for a new peer); set
# preshared_key = "" to remove one.
resource "edgeos_wireguard_peer" "office" {
  interface            = edgeos_wireguard_interface.wg0.name
  public_key           = "AgICAgICAgICAgICAgICAgICAgICAgICAgICAgICAgI="
  description          = "office"
  allowed_ips          = ["10.8.0.3/32", "192.168.50.0/24"]
  endpoint             = "vpn.example.com:51820"
  persistent_keepalive = 25
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `allowed_ips` (Set of String) Networks the peer may send from and that are routed to it, such as `10.8.0.2/32` or `0.0.0.0/0`.
- `interface` (String) WireGuard interface, usually `edgeos_wireguard_interface.x.name`. Changing it creates a new peer.
- `public_key` (String) The peer's base64 public key. It names the peer on the router, so changing it creates a new peer.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Free text description.
- `disabled` (Boolean) Keep the peer in the config but switch it off (the `disable` node). Defaults to `false`.
- `endpoint` (String) Where to reach the peer, as `host:port`, such as `vpn.example.com:51820`, `203.0.113.10:51820` or `[2001:db8::1]:51820`. Leave unset for road warriors that connect to the router.
- `persistent_keepalive` (Number) Send a keepalive every this many seconds, which keeps NAT mappings open. 25 is a common value.
- `preshared_key` (String, Sensitive) Optional preshared key for extra protection: the base64 key or an absolute path to a file on the router, such as `/config/auth/wg0-laptop.psk`. Leaving it out keeps whatever the router has, so an imported peer keeps its preshared key (and a new peer gets none). Set it to `""` to remove the preshared key from the peer. If the router hides the value from the API session, the configured value is kept in state.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<interface>:<public_key>`, for example `wg0:<base64 key>`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = edgeos_wireguard_peer.laptop
  id = "wg0:AQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQE="
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <interface>:<public key>
terraform import edgeos_wireguard_peer.laptop 'wg0:AQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQEBAQE='
```
